svg.title: DeltaV Live · Graphics Studio
svg.desc: Color-coded relationship map. Named containers show organization. Arrow labels describe creation, containment, references or calls. Select a card in the HTML atlas for its explanation and parser implications.
svg.text: Saved configuration model · functional groups, not a screenshot of the application
Configuration database → authoring views → saved items → publication → runtime
Displays · contextual displays · layouts · display sets

g.title: A GEM class defines a reusable object tree, exposed configuration properties and behavior. It can contain component GEM instances as well as shapes, text, data links and controls. Linked instances retain a class reference; unlinked GEMs do not track subsequent class edits.

Display, contextual-display and layout templates are library starting points used when creating new items. They cannot be published, tested online or referenced as runtime destinations. Template origin is different from the ongoing class reference of a linked GEM.

text.tspan: Creates new items; not ongoing class inheritance

g.title: Standards supply shared values such as colors, fonts, Booleans, images, strings, measurements and numbers. A property can reference a standard. Theme-specific values belong to standards; multilingual strings and ordinary strings serve different purposes.

text.tspan: Typed shared values; themes / languages as applicable
Color · font · image · Boolean · string · number…

g.title: Library functions transform inputs into typed results using value-based, rule-based or script-based logic. Referencing properties track that function. This is distinct from an arbitrary VBA procedure or an unrestricted TypeScript package import.

text.tspan: Inputs → conversion rules / expressions → typed result

g.title: A process display provides operator content. A contextual display is a reusable popup definition such as a faceplate or detail. A click can explicitly name a contextual display and pass a tag, or use Open Faceplate / Open Detail to follow the tag’s association.

text.tspan: Process displays; faceplates, details, custom popups
Contain placed GEM instances and other elements

g.title: An actual display, contextual display, layout or GEM class contains supported elements. Examples include groups, text, shapes, images, data links, controls and nested GEMs. Tabs/tab items organize content inside a display; they are not Explorer folders.

text.tspan: Groups · shapes · text · images · data links · controls
Nested GEMs / tabs; properties, events and bindings

g.title: A layout describes screen space. Screens represent monitors; display frames partition each screen and route displays by level or other configured rules. A frame presents a display; it is not the same thing as a group of shapes inside that display.

text.tspan: Arrange monitors / screen regions and route displays
Frames present content; they do not copy its objects

g.title: A display set lists displays and their navigation hierarchy. In the reviewed help, a hierarchy is at most four levels deep. A display can belong to multiple sets and appear at different levels in each; it appears at most once in one set.

text.tspan: The same display can have different levels by set

svg.text: These tools expose or execute configuration; they are not additional copies of every graphic.

g.title: Your Palette sketch is correct: it offers more than GEM classes. Built-in element groups and library GEMs are available according to the active configuration type. Dragging an item creates a placed element/instance on the canvas.

Shows properties of the selected item, organized into tabs and groups. GEM Configuration Designer creates the exposed custom-property schema; the Graphics Configuration pane is where a display engineer sees and sets those properties on an instance.

Saved configuration, published configuration and loaded runtime instances are distinct. Runtime evaluates bindings and executes configured event/timer actions. A contextual display timer is associated with the open configuration; it is not a controller-module scan.

text.tspan: Linked class edits deploy in displays

svg.text: Read arrows by their labels. The card inspector supplies additional relationships without drawing every dependency across the page.
